title: HTTP request and response
learningObjectives: Explain http request and response and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: HTTP is an application protocol based on requests and responses. A request includes a method, target, headers, and sometimes a body. A response includes a status code, headers, and an optional body. HTTP is stateless at the protocol level, while applications may use cookies or tokens to maintain sessions.
understand.whyItMatters: Understanding the exchange makes API debugging and frontend integration clearer. A response can arrive successfully at the transport level while carrying an error status.
understand.analogy: A request is a question sent to a service; a response is the service's answer with a status and supporting information.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The object models the parts of an HTTP exchange. Real headers and bodies are visible in browser developer tools.

examples.explanation: The object models the parts of an HTTP exchange. Real headers and bodies are visible in browser developer tools.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the concept; some browser examples require a real served page and supported APIs.

practise.guidedTask: Inspect a real GET and POST request in the Network panel. Identify method, status, headers, payload, and response body.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small web page. Record the expected behaviour, how you tested it, and any limitations or fallbacks.
hints: Use browser developer tools to inspect actual behaviour.
Test with keyboard and different viewport sizes.
Keep core content available when enhancements are unsupported.
